posts.title: The Gracious Hand of God
posts.excerpt: Nehemiah could have walked out of that throne room patting himself on the back. Instead he walked out with his eyes on the One who had been moving in the background.

posts.title: Remember Me
posts.excerpt: We all want to be seen. We all want our quiet faithfulness to count for something. Nehemiah just asked it of the only One who actually sees.

posts.title: 5 Signs You're Consuming Christian Content Instead of Actually Growing
posts.excerpt: A lot of us are consuming more than we ever have and growing less than we ever have. And the scary part is we do not always know the difference.

posts.title: When Fear Wears a Friendly Face
posts.excerpt: It is one thing when the bad guys are clearly the bad guys. It is harder when someone you trusted leans on your fear to push you out of obedience.

posts.title: They Read It and Went and Did It
posts.excerpt: They studied the Word, saw something they had been missing, and went and did it. No committee. No five-year plan. They just went.

posts.title: The Verse Without the Coffee Mug
posts.excerpt: Esther was not picking out a coffee mug. She was about to walk in to a king's throne room uninvited, knowing the law said she could be killed for it.
posts.verse: "If you keep quiet at a time like this, deliverance and relief for the Jews will arise from some other place, but you and your relatives will die. Who knows if perhaps you were made queen for just such a time as this?"
posts.description: Esther was facing death, not picking out wall art. The real such a time as this moments cost something. Most of us quote the verse but avoid the moment.

posts.title: Why I Highlighted This One
posts.excerpt: There is a part of me that reads this verse and thinks good. That is the honest answer. And I am not sure what to do with that.
posts.verse: "Afterward Mordecai returned to the palace gate, but Haman hurried home dejected and completely humiliated."
posts.description: Haman gets humbled and a part of me liked it. Sitting with the difference between God's justice and my flesh enjoying someone else's pain.

posts.title: Mercy Received
posts.excerpt: The Jews had just been rescued by God. And then the way they handled their new power scared everyone around them. Mercy received did not always become mercy given.
posts.verse: "The king took off his signet ring—which he had taken back from Haman—and gave it to Mordecai. And Esther appointed Mordecai to be in charge of Haman's property."
posts.description: God reversed everything for the Jews in Esther. But the verse hints they did not handle their new power with much mercy. A question for the rescued.

posts.title: Maybe I Have Had a Hard-Fought Hallelujah
posts.excerpt: Standing in church singing about a hard-fought hallelujah, I realized I actually have had a few. I just don't reach for them first when I think about my life.

posts.title: Job's Regular Practice
posts.excerpt: Long before Job lost everything, he was just a dad who got up early to intercede for his kids. Not panic prayer. A rhythm.
posts.verse: "When these celebrations ended—sometimes after several days—Job would purify his children. He would get up early in the morning and offer a burnt offering for each of them. For Job said to himself, 'Perhaps my children have sinned and have cursed God in their hearts.' This was Job's regular practice."
posts.description: Long before the suffering, Job was just a dad getting up early to cover his kids in prayer. Not panic prayer. A regular practice.

posts.title: While He Was Still Speaking
posts.excerpt: One messenger has not even finished before another shows up with worse news. And then another. The first thing Job did was fall on his face in worship.
posts.verse: "While he was still speaking, another messenger arrived with this news: 'The fire of God has fallen from heaven and burned up your sheep and all the shepherds. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.' While he was still speaking, another messenger arrived with this news: 'Three bands of Chaldean raiders have stolen your camels and killed your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.' While he was still speaking, another messenger arrived with this news: 'Your sons and daughters were feasting in their oldest brother's home...'"
posts.description: The messengers came faster than Job could process. He grieved and worshipped at the same time. What is in you when the messengers keep coming?

posts.title: How Can a Good God…?
posts.excerpt: Sitting in ashes, having lost everything, Job answers the most-asked question in the world in one sentence.
posts.verse: "But Job replied, 'You talk like a foolish woman. Should we accept only good things from the hand of God and never anything bad?' So in all this, Job said nothing wrong."
posts.description: Sitting in ashes, Job answers the most asked question in the world in one sentence. If we trust God with the good, we have to trust Him with the hard.

posts.title: If Only There Was a Mediator…
posts.excerpt: He could not have pictured a manger or a cross. But he felt the gap so deeply that he cried out for someone who could bring God and man together.
posts.verse: "If only there were a mediator between us, someone who could bring us together."
posts.description: Job did not know His name, but he felt the gap so deeply that he cried out for a mediator. Thousands of years later, that prayer was answered.

posts.title: Job 28:28
posts.excerpt: We talk a lot about wisdom. We rarely talk about where it actually comes from.
posts.verse: "And this is what he says to all humanity: ‘The fear of the Lord is true wisdom; to forsake evil is real understanding.’"
posts.description: Real wisdom starts with fearing God, and real understanding comes from actually walking away from what He calls wrong.

posts.title: Job 33:10
posts.excerpt: We go through a hard season and we start to make it about us in a way that is not even true.
posts.verse: "Yet God has found fault with me; he considers me his enemy."
posts.description: When we are suffering, it is easy to frame God as the enemy. Elihu called Job on it, and the correction is worth hearing.

posts.title: Job 42:3
posts.excerpt: He was not being sarcastic. He is not defeated. He is humbled. He is finally in the right place.
posts.verse: "You asked, 'Who is this that questions my wisdom with such ignorance?' It is I—and I was talking about things I knew nothing about, things far too wonderful for me."
posts.description: Job finally gets it — and his response teaches us what it looks like to stop demanding answers from God and start trusting Him instead.

posts.title: Job 42:17
posts.excerpt: Full does not mean happy every day. It does not mean easy. It means whole. Complete. Rounded out with everything a real life includes.
posts.verse: "Then he died, an old man who had lived a long, full life."
posts.description: The last verse of Job is almost too quiet for a book with so much drama. But that is exactly why it matters.

posts.title: Psalm 2:12
posts.excerpt: You bow to Him and find joy. Or you do not, and you get consumed by your own life.
posts.verse: "Submit to God's royal son, or he will become angry, and you will be destroyed in the midst of all your activities—for his anger flares up in an instant. But what joy for all who take refuge in him!"
posts.description: The whole verse boils down to a choice. Submit or not. Take refuge or not. There is no middle ground.

posts.title: Psalm 4:4
posts.excerpt: Sleep on it. And be quiet in the meantime. That is such practical wisdom. Especially the silent part.
posts.verse: "Don't sin by letting anger control you. Think about it overnight and remain silent."
posts.description: Anger controlling you is sin. But anger itself is not. There is a difference — and this verse tells you exactly what to do with it.

posts.title: Psalm 18:39
posts.excerpt: There have been seasons where I have had to be strong. Not because I found it in myself. Because God armed me with it.
posts.verse: "You have armed me with strength for the battle; you have subdued my enemies under my feet."
posts.description: He does not throw you into a battle empty handed. He equips you — and the strength shows up when the battle does.
